summary: The v1 map from the previous step was accepted (audit_spec_version 1, understanding_status usable), so this turn submits the first Candidate on that basis: a CandidateSubmission with action=obligation (draft/submission.json). It fixes one attributed follower-side responsibility over the principal Fact F-config - after appendEntries truncates a conflicting log suffix it resets only the latest configuration to the committed one (raft.go 1516-1531), leaving the committed configuration, the atomically published r.latestConfiguration copy and the retained log prefix unchanged. The obligation id is claim-config-rollback-consistency (concern consensus_safety, lifecycle recovery) and it is bound to the exact truncation site through binding bind-append-entries-truncate (material S-append-entries, symbol Raft.appendEntries, lines 1440-1584, verified Go declaration). The question is a ready_for_check direct_test over facts [F-config] with behaviors b-append-entries and b-config-change-append, backed by supporting behaviors b-request-vote and b-follower-heartbeat-timeout that consume the mutated latest configuration, so its activity context is A2 (core) plus A4. Grounding, applicability and counterevidence are kept distinct: no violation is asserted, the strongest sub-case (a conflict below the committed configuration index) is recorded as blocked on whether a legal sender can produce it, and the plausible benign alternative (the causing leader immediately re-replicates its own configuration entry) is retained as an unexplained alternative rather than suppressed. Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics. Next step is a formal check selecting the resulting Unit to observe, in a controlled cluster, whether a conflicting suffix containing a configuration entry leaves the follower's published and consumed configuration consistent with its retained log.
